marked_text: My sister wanted a practice upright before her recital in [[place]]Lisbon[[/]], so we spent Saturday copying what private sellers wanted for instruments that still had every key. A teacher in Alfama asked [[comp]]2360[[/]], a widow in Estrela asked [[comp]]3980[[/]], and a school closing a classroom asked [[comp]]1840[[/]]. The shop behind the tram barn wanted [[comp]]2870[[/]] for a German frame, a tuner in Santos wanted [[comp]]3520[[/]], and a church loft was listed at [[comp]]2100[[/]]. A damp basement piano stood at [[comp]]3140[[/]], and the last card on the cafe board was [[comp]]2590[[/]]. Benches stayed out of the talk.

ask.instruction: Give the euro amount sitting between the two central asking prices.

marked_text: The riad keeper in [[place]]Fez[[/]] wanted the courtyard zellige replaced before guests arrived, and he copied every mason onto the back of a sugar packet. The man from the tannery lane said [[comp]]1490[[/]]. A cousin offered [[comp]]780[[/]] if the old tiles could be lifted whole. The hotel contractor wrote [[comp]]2050[[/]]. A quieter crew from the medina put down [[comp]]1040[[/]], the tile merchant's brother said [[comp]]640[[/]], and a crew that brought its own cement said [[comp]]1760[[/]]. The remaining slips were [[comp]]1280[[/]] for labour only and [[comp]]910[[/]] if we carried the sand up ourselves.

marked_text: My uncle wanted a skiff and a skipper for one calm day out of [[place]]Split[[/]], and he made me write down what the harbour men asked. The blue hull wanted [[comp]]420[[/]], an older cousin said [[comp]]260[[/]] if we brought the fuel, the concrete pier asked [[comp]]510[[/]], and a man mending nets asked [[comp]]370[[/]]. No one included lunch.
